weakest.why: four sketches, no real user research yet
nothing on key loss, DID changes or a holder who loses the file

questions.question: What proofs should a certifiable URLU credential carry?
questions.why: The 1EdTech validator checks only the first proof, and JCS is not on its allowed list.

questions.question: Where does the issuer DID live?
options: A did:web on URLU's own domain, with did:web:trifold.app:orgs:urlu as an alias
questions.why: A DID on URLU's domain lets URLU leave Trifold; the alias covers orgs with no domain.

questions.question: Should our verifier accept other issuers' Open Badges?
options: Opt-in looser profile (more contexts, subject without id)
questions.why: Only 3 of 67 external samples verify today; Buzz clients may need to read other badges.

questions.question: Which license should tfd-credentials carry?
questions.why: The Buzz repo imports it, so it needs a clear license; the repo's own LICENSE is Apache-2.0.

questions.question: Pursue 1EdTech certification?
options: Request a dues quote now, certify when a buyer asks
questions.why: Dues depend on annual revenue and are unknown; the quote request costs nothing.

assumptions.text: 1EdTech's public validator uses the same checks as the official conformance suite.
The 1EdTech validator verifies only the first proof in a proof set (inferred from results, source not read).
A did:web on a real domain (no port) resolves in 1EdTech's validator; only localhost was tested.
The OB3 3.0.3 context copy at purl.imsglobal.org is authentic; no published digest exists to check it.

scope.text: Achievement credentials for Participant, Coach, Mediator
Bitstring status lists for revocation and suspension

acceptance.text: An achievement credential issued with issueCertifiable passes 1EdTech's public validator with no errors (an unreachable-issuer-URL warning is allowed).
issueCertifiable attaches an eddsa-rdfc-2022 proof by default and never lists eddsa-jcs-2022 first.
Changing any signed field, the context, the proof or the verification method is rejected by our verifier, the 1EdTech validator and DCC verifier-core.
Setting the revocation bit with put-if-match, then re-verifying, reports revoked in our verifier and the DCC verifier, and the 1EdTech validator raises a fatal revoked.
Verifying with no status resolver returns unchecked, never valid.
The public view omits the subject name unless the caller passes includeName.
The in-memory store and the ObjectStore adapter both pass the shared contract suites.
A suspended credential is reported suspended by our verifier and the DCC verifier; the 1EdTech validator's lack of suspension is documented.
The official 1EdTech conformance suite passes for an issuer using a real did:web domain.
A browser or Buzz client verifies a certificate using only the file, the issuer key document and an optional status list fetch.
The opt-in looser profile verifies the DCC and 1EdTech did:key sample credentials (3 of 67 verify today).
buzz-school's SQLite or Durable Object store passes statusListStoreContract.
The package declares a license and the Buzz repo can install it from a release tarball.

risks.text: The official 1EdTech suite differs from the public validator and fails us
risks.mitigation: Run the official suite early on a real did:web domain

risks.text: Children's data on a public verify page
risks.mitigation: Level, date and status only; counsel review before launch
Key rotation with kept key_ids; decide custody and key-revocation procedure
Use revocation for anything that must show there

risks.text: A replayed old status list looks current
risks.mitigation: Add validUntil to status lists or serve them with a short cache lifetime
